title: A Step-by-Step Procedure to Perform Preliminary Designs of Salient-Pole Synchronous Generators

source.citation: T. de P. M. Bazzo, V. de O. Moura, R. Carlson, Energies 14(16):4989, 2021
source.access: open access (CC BY 4.0); the PDF is cached locally (supplied for this replication)

machine.topology: inner salient-pole wound-field rotor (pole shoes with a concentric face, parallel pole bodies on a hexagonal core, field coils, four round damper bars per pole) in a 36-slot stator with trapezoidal slots and a double-layer lap winding pitched 5 of 6 slots
machine.symmetry: The whole cross-section is modelled (the paper's FEA modelled one pole, Fig. 10). A pole pitch negates every linkage at no load (half-wave symmetry); at balanced load currents the torque repeats every sixth of an electrical period (20 mechanical degrees).

components_map.part: stator: trapezoidal slots with parallel teeth, openings, wedges of their own and two coil layers stacked radially
components_map.component: trapezoidal_slot_stator (wedge closures and labels, layer divider: new)

components_map.part: double-layer lap winding pitched 5 of 6 slots, 13 turns per coil
salient-pole rotor: concentric pole faces, shoes, bodies on a hexagonal core, field coil blocks, damper bars, shaft, interpolar closures
field coils, 485 turns per pole, alternating polarity
steels from FEMM's library with their lamination fill
sliding band in the 3.5 mm gap
d/q inductances (two phases in series), load points and terminal quantities
components_map.component: step_statistic; dq_linkage (terminal quantities: new); phase_linkage (field-winding rotors: new)

slots.quote: It has been chosen to use 36 slots and double-layer lap windings

rotor_diameter_mm.note: The rotor's outer diameter at the pole faces; the face is concentric ("the air-gap between pole shoes and the internal diameter of stator is constant", Section 2.1).

shoe_straight_factor.note: Eq. (5): h_PSs = D_Re K_PSs / P = 6.25 mm.

coil_pitch_factor.note: Coils span 5 of the 6 slots of a pole pitch (Section 2.3.2: "the coil pitch is 5 slots").

coils_in_series.note: Eq. (30): T_A = T_Ac N_Cpp N_Cs = 13 x 2 x 6 = 156 turns per phase, every coil of a phase in series.

field_current_nl_A.note: The no-load field current (Fig. 12's caption: "field current equal to I_Fnl").

field_current_fl_A.note: The full-load field current (Table 5's 100% row); see the gap on how the full-load FEA was driven.

shoe_width_mm.note: The chord between the face corners: eq. (3) gives D_Re sin(K_aP alpha_P / 2) = 85.505 mm.

shoe_height_mm.note: From the rotor surface on the pole axis to the flat underside; eqs. (2), (5), (6) give 7.538 + 6.25 = 13.788 mm, the table's value 0.022 mm more (it fixes the underside).

pole_body_height_mm.note: Recorded: the build takes the core from eq. (8)'s apothem (below), so its body is 37.136 mm.

field_turns_per_pole.note: Per pole: eq. (10) counts the turns that fit one coil side's window (h_PB W_PBc K_Ff / S_F = 37.14 x 27.21 x 0.8 / 1.6667 = 485.1), and eqs. (11)-(13) give the design's B_PB = 1.25 T only with 485 x 2.5 A per pole. Control field-turns-total (485 in all: 81 per pole).

stator_bore_diameter_mm.note: Eq. (14): D_Re + 2 L_AG with L_AG = 3.5 mm.

slot_width_top_mm.note: At the wedge's end, D_St/2 = 132.74 mm from the axis.

slot_height_mm.note: The slot body below the wedge (eq. (20)).

stator_outer_diameter_mm.note: Recorded: the build closes the radial build (eq. (23)) at 349.62 mm.

damper_bars_per_pole.quote: Number of damper bars per pole 4

rated_current_A.note: The design's armature current (rms), the nominal current of the inductance test.

armature_resistance_ohm.note: At 100 C; eqs. (36)-(40) with r_Akm 3.92 ohm/km reproduce it (0.628).

steel_grade.reason: The paper names no steel; its loss data (1.656 W/kg hysteresis and 0.698 W/kg eddy current, from Grauers) are a 2.35 W/kg-class non-oriented lamination (M235-35A to M250-35A), whose FEMM equivalent is AISI M-19 at 14 mil (0.36 mm); the library entry carries its lamination fill (0.955). The rotor poles and core are taken to be of the same laminations (rotor_steel_grade).
steel_grade.note: Pre-solve estimate: M-45 18 mil -0.6% in B_PB, fill 1 +0.2%, solid 1010 -6.4%.

steel_fill.reason: The library entry's own lamination fill for 14 mil M-19; the paper states none.

rotor_steel_grade.reason: Small salient-pole generators stack their poles (and usually the core) from laminations; the same grade as the stator.
rotor_steel_grade.note: Pre-solve estimate: a solid 1010 rotor under the M-19 stator lowers B_PB 3.1%.

shaft_material.reason: Fig. 10 shows nothing inside the core's inner arc; a non-magnetic shaft (or none).
shaft_material.note: Pre-solve estimate: 0.03% in B_PB (the core carries about 0.45 T).

wedge_mu_r.reason: Fig. 2 draws the slot wedge as a part of its own; no magnetic wedge is named.

test_current_A.reason: "Excited with nominal armature current": Table 6's rated current, 21.66 A rms, carried as a static current in the two phases in series.
test_current_A.note: Pre-solve estimate: its peak (30.63 A) saturates the d axis, L_d about -5%.

fea_id_rms_A.figure: Fig. 14, p. 19 (vector art): the I_d curve's centreline, averaged over 0-180 degrees
fea_id_rms_A.scale_reference: the figure's 16 horizontal gridlines at 5 A (fit residual at most 0.12 A)
fea_id_rms_A.note: On the paper's phasor scale (rms: |I_dq| = 21.13 A, the phase currents' fundamental 21.11 A); positive I_d demagnetizes (Fig. 6, generator convention). The design's 100% point has 17.135 A.

fea_iq_rms_A.figure: Fig. 14, p. 19 (vector art): the I_q curve's centreline, averaged over 0-180 degrees
fea_iq_rms_A.scale_reference: the figure's 16 horizontal gridlines at 5 A (fit residual at most 0.12 A)
fea_iq_rms_A.note: In phase with the EMF (generating). The design's 100% point has 13.25 A.

band_margin_mm.reason: Thin air between the sliding band and each gap surface (a 2.5 mm band in the 3.5 mm gap).

gap_arc_deg.reason: Arc pieces of the band, the pole faces and the bore (0.55 mm).

thin_air_mesh_mm.reason: The thin gap layers and the slot openings joined to them.

stator_iron_mesh_mm.reason: Stator teeth (11.6 mm) and yoke (24.9 mm).

slot_arc_deg.reason: Arc pieces of the damper bars and the shaft.

outer_arc_deg.reason: Arc pieces of the stator's outer circle (3 mm).

shoe_tip_height_mm.note: From the face corners to the underside that Table 3's h_PS fixes (6.270 mm; eq. (5)'s h_PSs is 6.25).

core_apothem_mm.note: Eq. (8)'s apothem: the hexagonal core's flat under each pole lies where the interpolar axes cross the shoe's chord half-width, so neighbouring coils meet at its corners (74.054 mm; Table 3's heights give 74.05).

field_coil_width_mm.note: Eq. (7)'s W_PBc: the coil fills the body side up to the shoe tips' line (27.21 mm).

damper_pitch_deg.note: K_Dp alpha_S = 8 degrees (Fig. 10: 8.11 +/- 0.10); eq. (55) as printed, alpha_S (1 - K_Dp), gives 2 degrees, which cannot place four bars on the 40 degree shoe.

layer_divider_height_mm.note: Equal areas for the two coil layers (each holds one 13-turn coil side; Fig. 2's separator crosses the slot near its middle): 9.09 mm below the slot top.

fea_id_peak_A.note: Amplitude-invariant peak, currents into the terminals: demagnetizing.

gaps.item: whether the 485 field turns are per pole or in total
gaps.affects: every field-driven quantity, by a factor of six
gaps.note: Per pole: eq. (10) fills one coil side's window, and eqs. (11)-(13) reproduce the design's 1.25 T only with 485 turns per pole; the pre-solve estimate gives 1.27 T per pole and 0.21 T for 485 in total against the FEA's 1.28 T. Control field-turns-total (81 per pole). The paper's field resistance and copper loss are then one pole coil's (a finding).

gaps.item: the steel grade and B-H curve
gaps.affects: B_PB, the EMF and the full-load torque by up to about 6%; L_d by about 2%
gaps.note: M-19 14 mil (library fill 0.955) in stator and rotor, the equivalent of the 2.35 W/kg-class lamination the loss data describe. Bracketed before freezing (pre-solve estimate, B_PB): M-45 18 mil -0.6%, fill 1 +0.2%, solid 1010 -6.4%, a solid 1010 rotor -3.1%. The electrical steels lie within the tolerance; the solid steels do not, and are controls (steel-1010, rotor-solid-1010) with steel-m45 and steel-fill-1.

gaps.affects: the core's flux density (about 0.45 T), negligibly
gaps.note: The core's outer shape is eq. (8)'s hexagon (apothem 74.05 mm); its inner diameter, D_Ri, is not tabulated: Fig. 10's inner arc gives 56.4 +/- 0.6 mm. Inside it non-magnetic (assumed, control shaft-steel; estimate 0.03%).

gaps.item: the damper bars' depth, pitch and material
gaps.affects: the pole shoe's iron near the face, slightly
gaps.note: Fig. 10: centres 121.95 +/- 0.25 mm from the axis (3.04 mm under the face), 8.11 +/- 0.10 degrees apart; the build takes K_Dp alpha_S = 8 degrees (eq. (55) as printed gives 2). Copper (eq. (57)); in static solves they carry no current.

gaps.item: how the full-load FEA was driven
gaps.note: A time-stepping FEA with saturation (Section 3), its field current not restated (Table 2's I_F = 4.78 A, the design's full-load value, is taken) and its armature connected to a load the paper does not describe (its currents carry an 8.4% 3rd harmonic, so the load's neutral was connected). The replication drives FEMM with the FEA's own fundamental currents, Fig. 14's Park components, and compares the torque (acceptance) and the terminal quantities (comparators, with no external elements and with the design's R_A and L_Tend). Table 5's load points test the design model at its own currents and field currents (comparators).

gaps.item: the inductance test current (nominal armature current: rms or peak)
gaps.note: 21.66 A rms carried as a static current; control test-current-peak (30.63 A).

gaps.affects: slot leakage and the gap permeance, slightly

gaps.note: Fig. 2 draws a separator across the slot: the two coil sides lie one above the other; equal areas for equal turns.

gaps.item: the rotor position of the paper's B_PB and of its time steps
gaps.affects: the slot ripple of B_PB and the torque
gaps.note: Means over the positions of a period: the paper reports one value without its instant.

findings: Failed: one of six acceptance values passes, the winding sign and phase order against the construction (phases within 0.002 electrical degrees of the field-winding prediction, amplitudes within 7e-6). Every FE value the paper gives is missed by 7-13%, the no-load ones high and the full-load torque low: B_PB 1.3825 T against 1.28 (+8.0%), L_d 44.36 mH against 40.78 (+8.8%), L_q 27.84 against 26.10 (+6.7%), the no-load EMF fundamental 259.77 V against Fig. 12's 230.51 (+12.7%), and the full-load mean torque 119.69 N m against 131.6 (-9.1%; Fig. 15: 131.73). The mesh is settled (0.75: 190k elements, 1.4: 107k, all within 0.1%; a 2.5 times coarser diagnostic, 97k, the same), and the stress-tensor and flux-linkage torques agree (119.69, 119.62).

What matches: the shapes. The L_2ps sweep peaks on the d axis and bottoms on the q axis like Fig. 7 (its ratio 1.594 against 1.562); the no-load EMF's THD is the FEA's, 7.1% (Fig. 12: 7.1%; 3rd harmonic 5.5% against 5.3%, 13th 3.0% against 2.75%); the full-load torque ripple is 32.2 against 34.8 N m peak to peak (comparator passed at 30%) though the FEA's currents carried a 9% THD; and the inductances from single-axis currents (44.01 and 28.01 mH) confirm the two-phase definition's (44.36, 27.84) within 1%.
The field-turn reading is confirmed: with 485 turns in total (81 per pole) B_PB is 0.221 T and the EMF 44.5 V (control field-turns-total), against 1.28 T and 230.5 V; the paper's 485 are per pole.

The assumed inputs' controls bracket the miss without closing it. Steel: M-45 (18 mil) moves B_PB, the EMF and the inductances by under 0.8% and the torque to -7.6%; solid M-19 (fill 1) raises the no-load values (B_PB +9.5%, EMF +14.2%) and the torque to -6.4%; solid hot-rolled 1010 throughout, the low end of the bracket, comes closest: B_PB +2.6%, L_d +2.0%, L_q +3.0%, EMF +6.4%, torque -6.7% (the pre-solve estimate said -6.4% in B_PB; FEMM gave -5.1%); a solid 1010 rotor under M-19: +4.5, +5.0, +5.3, +9.1% and -5.3%. The inductance test at the nominal current's peak lowers L_d to 43.43 and L_q to 27.54 mH (+6.5, +5.5%). A steel shaft changes nothing (under 0.01%); magnetic wedges (mu_r 5) raise the inductances by 19-23%. No control passes any FE target.

The full-load point shows how the FEA's machine differs. Driven by the FEA's own currents, FEMM's internal voltage is V_d = 73.3 and V_q = 231.1 V (rms) against Fig. 13's 104.9 and 210.4: its q-axis inductance under load is V_d / (w I_q) = 18.3 mH, a third below its 27.8 mH without field current (M-19's cross-saturation, the pole body at 1.48 T), whereas the FEA's V_d gives 26.3 mH (28 mH if its circuit held 0.44 ohm), its own no-field L_q: the FEA's iron hardly saturates at full load (Fig. 11 shows the pole body at 1.2-1.4 T). FEMM's power factor is 0.815 against 0.89, its line voltage 420.0 V without and 393.4 V with the design's R_A and L_Tend against 405.98 (comparators). The FEA's output (13.21 kW) is 0.59 kW below its torque times speed (13.80 kW): losses in its circuit and bars, about 0.44 ohm per phase if all copper, between the design's 20 C winding (0.48 ohm) and its active length alone (0.32).

Diagnostics outside the frozen case (bazzo/diag, 20-solve reductions of the case's steps; the base reproduces the run within 0.1%, its 6-position torque within 0.4%) read the signature. A longer gap lowers all four no-load values together (+0.25 mm: B_PB +3.5%, EMF +7.2%, L_d +2.6%, L_q +2.1%; +0.5 mm: -1.0, +1.7, -2.8, -1.9%) but lowers the torque further (-11.8%, -14.1%); Fig. 10 shows the drawn gap at 3.52 +/- 0.1 mm. Another full-load field current cannot give both voltages: 4.0 A gives 106.5 N m and V_q 175.7 V, 5.5 A 125.7 N m and 258.7 V. Linear iron (no B-H curve) restores the FEA's q axis: at mu_r 600 V_d is 104.4 V (-0.5%), the EMF +0.4%, L_q -0.5% and the torque +3.8%, but B_PB -4.1%, L_d -4.5% and V_q +12.7%; mu_r 1000 gives +1.9, +7.0, +0.9, +2.5% and +9.9% in torque. Linear iron with a longer gap (mu_r 2000, +0.6 mm) gives the torque within 0.2% but B_PB -6.1% and L_d -7.4%. No single input, and no pair tried, reproduces the no-load values and the load point together. The FEA's iron model is the most likely seat of the difference (the paper names no steel, and its FEA behaves as if its iron hardly saturated while its no-load flux is lower than any library steel gives); it stays a reviewed failure.

Table 5's analytic load points, as comparators: at the design's field currents and currents (PF 0.9 and its load angles) FEMM gives 441.8, 426.9, 408.9, 389.9 and 369.6 V line to line at 25, 50, 75, 100 and 125% load against the 400 V the design model holds, with R_A and L_Tend outside the 2D model: the linear design model (E proportional to I_F, constant X_d and X_q) misses saturation and cross-saturation, which take 70 V off between light and 125% load. At the design's rated point the output is 12.15 kW against 13.50 and the line voltage 389.9 against 400.3; the design's B_PB (1.25 T, no iron, no leakage) is 10.6% below FEMM's.

The paper's own procedure has three slips the replication found by recomputing its tables: eq. (29) yields Table 3's 156 turns per phase only with eq. (28)'s distribution factor taken at the mechanical slot angle (0.9962 instead of 0.9659), so the design's EMF (230.9 V at I_Fnl) is 3% optimistic; eq. (55) prints the damper pitch as alpha_S (1 - K_Dp), 2 degrees, where Fig. 10 and the four bars need K_Dp alpha_S = 8; and eq. (41) with the 485 turns per pole gives one pole coil's resistance, so Table 3's 3.80 ohm and Table 4's 87.5 W field loss are a sixth of the field winding's (22.8 ohm, 521 W at 4.78 A). Table 3's h_PS (13.81 mm) is 0.02 mm above eqs. (2), (5), (6).

retrospective: Time (IST): reading the paper and its figures about 30 minutes (Figs. 7 and 12-15 are vector art, read on their gridlines to 0.05 mH, 1 V and 0.05 A; Fig. 10 is a 464 px raster read at its native resolution for the shaft and damper bars); the new rotor component, the stator options, the field-winding linkage and the dq terminal quantities with their tests about 15 minutes; the generator, pre-solve estimate and freeze about 20 minutes (frozen 15:57); the timed first solve and its fix 2 minutes; run1, the article and ten controls, about 2 h 45 min of solving (139 solves a level at 6-10 s, 107-190k elements); the 14 designs re-run (15 minutes) and the signature diagnostics (40 minutes) ran beside it.

What decided the outcome was visible before freezing and not acted on. The host-side magnetic circuit gave an EMF of 258 V at the no-load field current, within 1% of FEMM's 259.8 V and 12% above the paper's FEA; it was set aside as crude because the paper's design EMF (230.9 V) and its FEA (230.5 V) agreed. They agree because the design carries a 0.89 leakage factor and a 3% slip in its distribution factor, not because a model of the drawn machine gives 230 V. Proposed for SKILL.md (stage 3): compare the pre-solve estimate with the paper's FE values, not only with its design values; when the estimate misses an FE value by more than its own spread over the assumed inputs, record the expected miss in the coverage before freezing, and look for the input that could close it (here only the iron model could, and the paper names no steel).

The steel bracket was taken at no load (B_PB within 0.6% across electrical steels) and missed the load point, where M-19's cross-saturation takes a third off L_q and 9% off the torque. Proposed for SKILL.md (stage 3): bracket an assumed material at every operating point the targets use, the load point's q axis included, and read the reference's own load-point equations (V_d = X_q I_q - R I_d) for what its FEA implies (here an unsaturated L_q under load).

The skill had no rule for a design paper whose FEA runs into a load it does not describe. Driving FEMM with the FEA's own Park currents (read from vector art) made the torque an acceptance target independent of the circuit; the terminal quantities stayed comparators with and without the external elements. Proposed for SKILL.md (stage 4, reference angles): when the paper plots its FEA's d- and q-axis currents, impose them and compare torque; check them against the phase currents' fundamental first.

Lessons that held: vector figures read exactly (Fig. 7's extremes halve to Table 3's inductances within 0.01 mH; Fig. 14's dq magnitude is the phase currents' fundamental); an overlay of the build on the authors' FE plot settled the coils, core corners, damper bars and shaft; the timed first solve (one step of each kind) caught a metric that divided by zero before it cost a level; reading the discrepancy's signature with single-input diagnostics separated a gap-like no-load excess from a saturation-like load deficit. A lesson that did not settle it: a uniform factor points at a scale - here the no-load factors (1.07-1.13) were not uniform and the load torque went the other way, so no scale, gap, field current or steel reproduced the paper, and no pair tried did.

The area-based element estimate missed by three times again (50k against 147,575) despite the 2.5 per h^2 rule: fine arcs on four gap circles dominate. Proposed: count elements along fine arcs as (arc length / piece length) x (layers of the thinnest adjoining region) before the area terms, or always size solves_per_process from the timed first solve, as here.

Generic changes: salient_pole_rotor (pole shoes with concentric or eccentric faces, straight tips and flat undersides, polygon or round cores, field coil blocks sharing the polygon's corners, damper bars, shaft, interpolar closures) with its knowledge record, tests and the synthetic design design-wound-field-salient-pole; trapezoidal_slot_stator wedge closures and labels and a radial layer divider; linkage_prediction for wound-field rotors (the field coils' current distribution as the rotor's source); dq_linkage terminal quantities (v_d, v_q, line voltage, electrical power and terminal power factor with an external resistance and end-winding inductance) and a scale; the schema's wfsm family. Lessons on wound-field construction, metric restriction and element counts, recomputing a design paper's tables from its equations, driving an undisclosed load with the FEA's own currents, and reading the iron's saturation from a load point.

A winding-function estimate gives L_d 41.7 mH unsaturated, about 41.0 with the iron at 21.66 A (the paper: 40.78) and about -5% at the 30.63 A peak; L_q about 20 mH (crude interpolar term; the paper 26.10). The full-load torque from the paper's own L_d, L_q and the unsaturated EMF at 4.78 A is 132.2 N m (FEA 131.6). About 50k elements (thin gap layers 12k, stator iron 10-14k, rotor iron 8-11k, coils 6k, openings 3k): 139 solves per level, 11 levels. The timed first solve meshed 147,575 elements (6 s per solve).
